value.string: relative_url, count_only=False, filters={}, listbox_id=\'listbox\', max_records=500, query=None, select_list=[], sort_on=None, view=\'view\'

Collect rows from a document's listbox - or from a REPORT - with automatic pagination.
 
 Reads a document, finds its listbox, and pages through the rows. Returns flat
 row data (not full document details - use erp5_read on individual rows for that).
 
 Rows come from the module's OWN list_method, so this is what the module itself
 shows: its default parameters (section scope, portal types) still apply and
 related keys resolve. Filter with 'filters' (column criteria, ranges, LIKE
 wildcards) rather than 'query' for anything field-specific, and count with
 count_only=true.
 
 A REPORT COMES BACK HERE AS ROWS, NOT AS A FILE.
 Report actions are the names in the 'reports' array of erp5_read and
 erp5_inspect, e.g. 'global_stock_report' on product_module. A report is a table
 sitting behind a parameter dialog: pass the report action name as 'view' and
 this tool follows that dialog to the form which really holds the rows.
 
 erp5_collect(relative_url="product_module", view="global_stock_report")
 
 The answer then carries 'report' (which dialog was followed to which form),
 'list_method' and 'list_method_parameters' - the parameter names the report's
 own script accepts. Pass those in 'filters' under exactly those names; the
 dialog's your_* widgets are only the UI spelling of the same things. When a
 report declares count/offset parameters, that is how you page through it -
 this tool's own max_records only caps how many rows it collects in one call.
 
 USE THIS WHEN:
 - You need ALL rows from a listbox (e.g. all posts in a thread, all events on a ticket).
 - You want a report's numbers as a table: view=<report action name>.
 - You want to filter or sort listbox contents.
 - You are filtering or reading a column the module SHOWS in its listbox, such as a
 related key (e.g. accounting_transaction_mirror_section_title) or a date like
 operation_date - the plain catalog behind erp5_search cannot serve those.
 - The listbox has more rows than a single page shows.
 
 DO NOT USE THIS WHEN:
 - You need the full document tree with nested children - use erp5_read_deep instead.
 erp5_collect returns flat rows; erp5_read_deep returns a recursive tree.
 - You want to search ACROSS modules - use erp5_search with no relative_url.
 - You want a report or export as a FILE (PDF/ODS/XLSX) rather than as rows -
 use erp5_download.
 
 PREREQUISITE: either the view has a listbox (erp5_read lists it under
 'all_listboxes'), or 'view' is a report action name from the 'reports' array.
 On a report dialog erp5_read answers all_listboxes: null and explains under
 'dialog' where the rows are - that is expected and does not mean there are
 none. erp5_inspect lists the column names accepted by filters/sort_on.
